# 1 Maccabees Chapter 11 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_011_page_001.jpg

---

**1** The king of Egypt assembled a great army, as many as the sand on the seashore, and many ships; for he was scheming by treachery to seize Alexander's kingdom and add it to his own.

**2** He traveled into Syria with friendly overtures, and the people of the cities opened their gates to him and went out to meet him, because Alexander the king had ordered them to meet him, since he was his father-in-law.

**3** But as Ptolemy entered each city, he installed a garrison of troops.

**4** When he came near Azotus, they showed him the burned-out temple of Dagon and the ruins of Azotus and its suburbs, with bodies strewn about — those whom Jonathan had burned in the war, for they had piled them along his route.

**5** They reported to the king what Jonathan had done, hoping to discredit him, but the king kept silence.

**6** Jonathan met the king at Joppa with pomp; they exchanged greetings and lodged there.

**7** Jonathan accompanied the king to the river called Eleutherus, then returned to Jerusalem.

**8** King Ptolemy seized the coastal cities as far as Seleucia-by-the-Sea, all the while plotting evil against Alexander.

**9** He sent envoys to King Demetrius, saying: "Come, let us make a treaty; I will give you my daughter, whom Alexander now has, and you shall reign over your father's kingdom.

**10** For I regret having given Alexander my daughter, since he sought to kill me."

**11** He slandered Alexander because he coveted his kingdom.

**12** He took his daughter away from Alexander and gave her to Demetrius; and Ptolemy broke with Alexander, and their enmity became open.

**13** Ptolemy entered Antioch and put on the crown of Asia; thus he wore two crowns — the crown of Egypt and the crown of Asia.

**14** King Alexander was in Cilicia at that time, because the people of that region were in revolt.

**15** When Alexander heard this, he came to make war on Ptolemy; Ptolemy led out his army, met him with a strong force, and routed him.

**16** Alexander fled to Arabia to seek shelter there, and King Ptolemy was exalted.

**17** Zabdiel the Arab cut off Alexander's head and sent it to Ptolemy.

**18** But King Ptolemy died three days later, and the garrisons in the fortresses were destroyed by those inside the fortresses.

**19** Demetrius became king in the one hundred and sixty-seventh year.

**20** In those days Jonathan mustered the men of Judea to attack the citadel in Jerusalem, and they constructed many siege engines against it.

**21** Some lawless men who hated their own people went to the king and reported that Jonathan was besieging the citadel.

**22** The king was angry when he heard this, and as soon as he heard it he came to Ptolemais and wrote to Jonathan, ordering him to stop the siege and to come to him immediately.

**23** When Jonathan heard this, he ordered the siege to continue; he then selected some of the elders of Israel and some priests and took a risk.

**24** He took silver, gold, clothing, and many other gifts and went to the king at Ptolemais, where he found favor in the king's eyes.

**25** Though certain lawless men of his nation made accusations against him,

**26** the king treated Jonathan just as his predecessors had; he honored him in the sight of all his friends,

**27** and confirmed him in the high priesthood and in all his other previous dignities, and had him registered as one of the king's chief friends and awarded him first rank.

**28** Jonathan then petitioned the king to make Judea free from tribute and the three districts, promising three hundred talents in exchange.

**29** The king agreed and wrote Jonathan letters concerning all these matters, as follows:

**30** "King Demetrius to his brother Jonathan and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.

**31** We are sending you a copy of the letter we wrote to Lasthenes our kinsman about you, so that you may know it.

**32** King Demetrius to Lasthenes his father, greetings.

**33** We have decided to show favor to the nation of the Jews, who are our friends and fulfill their obligations to us, because of the goodwill they bear us.

**34** We have confirmed to them the territory of Judea and the three districts of Aphaerema, Lydda, and Ramathaim, which were added to Judea from Samaria with all their dependencies, for all who offer sacrifice in Jerusalem, in place of the royal revenues that the king previously received from them annually from the produce of the land and from the fruit of the trees.

**35** As for the other dues that henceforth belong to us — the tithes and tolls that are owed to us, and the salt pits, and the crown taxes — we grant all these to them as a release.

**36** Not one of these provisions shall be annulled from this time and forever.

**37** Take care, therefore, to have a copy of this made and given to Jonathan, to be placed on the holy mountain in a conspicuous place."

**38** When King Demetrius saw that the land was quiet before him and no one resisted him, he dismissed all his forces, each man to his own place, except for the foreign mercenaries he had recruited from the islands of the nations; so all the veteran troops of his predecessors hated him.

**39** Now there was a certain man named Trypho, who had previously been on Alexander's side. Seeing that all the army was grumbling against Demetrius, he went to Imalkue the Arab, who was raising Antiochus the young son of Alexander.

**40** He pressed him, saying: "Hand Antiochus over to me so that he may become king in his father's place." He told him all that Demetrius had done and the hostility his troops bore him; and he stayed there many days.

**41** Jonathan sent a request to King Demetrius that he remove the garrison of the citadel from Jerusalem and the troops from the strongholds, because they were constantly fighting against Israel.

**42** Demetrius sent back to Jonathan: "Not only will I do this for you and your people, but I will greatly honor you and your people when the opportunity presents itself.

**43** For now, do me this favor and send me men to fight for me, for all my forces have mutinied."

**44** Jonathan sent three thousand valiant men to Antioch; they came to the king, and the king was overjoyed at their arrival.

**45** The people of the city — about one hundred and twenty thousand men — had massed together and wanted to kill the king.

**46** The king fled into the palace while the city's people seized the main streets of the city and began to attack.

**47** The king called the Jews to his aid; they rallied to him at once and spread through the city, and they killed about one hundred thousand men that day.

**48** They set the city ablaze, seized much plunder that day, and rescued the king.

**49** When the city's people saw that the Jews had gained control of the city as they wished, their resolve collapsed and they cried out to the king in supplication:

**50** "Grant us peace and make the Jews stop fighting against us and the city."

**51** The king laid down his arms and made peace. The Jews were honored before the king and before all in his kingdom, and they returned to Jerusalem with much plunder.

**52** So King Demetrius sat secure on his throne and the land was quiet before him.

**53** But he broke every promise he had made and estranged himself from Jonathan; he did not repay him for the services Jonathan had rendered but treated him very harshly.

**54** After this, Trypho returned, and with him the young Antiochus; Antiochus was crowned and took the diadem.

**55** All the forces that Demetrius had dismissed rallied to Antiochus; they fought against Demetrius, and he fled and was routed.

**56** Trypho captured the elephants and took possession of Antioch.

**57** The young Antiochus wrote to Jonathan: "I confirm you in the high priesthood and appoint you over the four districts, and you are to be one of the king's friends."

**58** He sent him golden vessels and a table service and gave him the right to drink from golden cups and wear purple and wear a golden brooch.

**59** His brother Simon he appointed governor from the Ladder of Tyre to the borders of Egypt.

**60** Jonathan set out and traveled through the cities of the Trans-Euphrates and all the Syrian forces joined him as allies; he came to Ashkelon and the people of the city received him with honor.

**61** From there he went to Gaza, but the people of Gaza shut their gates against him; he besieged it and burned its outskirts and plundered them.

**62** Then the men of Gaza appealed to Jonathan, and he gave them his right hand; he took the sons of their rulers as hostages and sent them off to Jerusalem, then traveled through the country as far as Damascus.

**63** Jonathan heard that the officers of Demetrius had come with a large army to Kedesh in Galilee, intending to remove him from his position.

**64** He went to meet them, leaving his brother Simon in charge of the country.

**65** Simon encamped against Beth-zur, attacked it for many days, and blockaded it.

**66** They appealed to him for terms; he granted their request, but expelled them from the city, which he then seized and placed under garrison.

**67** Jonathan and his army encamped beside the waters of Gennesareth; early in the morning they marched to the plain of Hazor.

**68** There before them in the plain was the army of the foreigners; they had set an ambush in the hills, while they themselves advanced to meet Jonathan head-on.

**69** Those in ambush burst out from their positions and joined the attack; all those with Jonathan fled,

**70** not one remaining except Mattathias son of Absalom and Judas son of Chalphi, commanders of the forces.

**71** Jonathan tore his clothes, put earth on his head, and prayed.

**72** Then Jonathan turned back against his enemies and routed them, and they fled.

**73** When the men who had fled from him saw this, they turned back and joined him in pursuit as far as Kedesh, to the enemy camp, and they encamped there.

**74** About three thousand of the foreigners fell that day; and Jonathan returned to Jerusalem.
